title: perf-regression-triage-playbook
content:
Purpose:
This is a working playbook for diagnosing serving-runtime performance regressions: alerts from dashboards, triage steps, bisect techniques, and canary-vs-prod comparisons. Target audience: eng-serving-runtime oncall, SREs, and perf engineers.

Scope:
- Latency regressions (P50/P95/P99 increases)
- Throughput regressions (requests/sec drop, increased queueing)
- Increased tail latency due to GC, kernel changes, or model code changes
- Regressions introduced by infra, kernel, CUDA, runtime, or model changes

High-level workflow (quick):
1) Alert -> gather context (dashboard, scope, affected routes/models)
2) Reproduce in canary / isolated environment if possible
3) Capture traces, profiles, and resource metrics (CPU/GPU/network/IO)
4) Bisect candidate commits/configs if repro is narrow to a rollout
5) Mitigate (rollback, route around, scale-up) and follow with root cause analysis

Initial data to collect (always):
- Alert id / Grafana panel / time window
- Affected model(s) / route(s) / customer ids (if available)
- Exact metric(s) regressed (e.g., P95 latency for route X increased from 90ms -> 230ms)
- Recent deploys: canary tag, commit SHAs, runtime image versions, kernel updates, CUDA/driver versions
- Canary vs prod comparison URL(s) and times

Useful dashboards / queries (PromQL examples):
- P95 latency for route: histogram_quantile(0.95, sum(rate(http_request_duration_seconds_bucket{route="/generate"}[5m])) by (le))
- Request queue length: avg_over_time(serving_queue_length{pool="gpu-pool-a"}[5m])
- GPU util: avg_over_time(nvidia_gpu_utilization[1m])
- KV-cache hit rate: sum(rate(kv_cache_hits_total[5m])) / sum(rate(kv_cache_requests_total[5m]))

Triage checklist (step-by-step):
1) Confirm alert validity
   - Check alerting thresholds and panel times. Is this transient or sustained?
   - Cross-check with SLO/Incidents channel.
2) Scope blast radius
   - Which clusters/regions/pools are affected? Use tags: cluster, region, pool.
   - Is the regression across all models or a subset?
3) Canary vs Prod comparison
   - Compare same time window. If canary shows the regression, we narrow to recent rollout.
   - Use Grafana "compare" panel and our canary tagging labels.
4) Quick mitigations
   - If a recent canary is culprit: rollback to previous stable canary.
   - If due to capacity: temporarily scale up dedicated pool or enable burst capacity.
   - If causing customer outages: create incident and notify CS.
5) Deeper repro & profiling
   - Reproduce on a small scale: run the same load against canary and stable: rwd-bench --concurrency 16 --seq-len 512 --route /generate --model gptx-v1 --target http://canary-host:8080
   - Collect pprof and tracing: curl http://host:6060/debug/pprof/profile?seconds=30 -> upload to perf-s3 and check flamegraph.
   - If native code suspected, capture perf or AMD/Intel counters and GPU traces (nsys/nsight for CUDA kernels).
   - Capture heap/GC profiles for JVM/python: Java Flight Recorder (JFR) or py-spy / tracemalloc.

Bisect process (when suspecting code change):
- If suspect is a single service repo: run git bisect between last-known-good and bad commit using perf microbench harness. Steps:
  1) Identify good/bad SHAs from deploy timeline.
  2) Use bisect harness: scripts/bisect_perf.sh --good=<good_sha> --bad=<bad_sha> --benchmark=integration-latency --runs=5
  3) Harness will auto-deploy or run containerized tests and report the commit where performance changed.
- If bisect shows noisy results, increase sample size or run under isolated hardware to reduce variance.

Canary comparisons (practical tips):
- Always compare same load profile and warmup state. Cold-start differences are common — ensure caches warmed (run 1000 warmup requests).
- Compare KV cache hit rates, prefix cache sizes — small changes in tokenization or attention can impact cache utilization.
- Check model quantization/profile diffs (e.g., model compiled with 8-bit kernel change).

Profiling checklist (what to gather):
- Aggregated metrics: p50/p95/p99, qps, errors, retries, queue_length, backpressure signals
- Host-level: CPU, memory, disk IO, network, ephemeral storage (bursting), kernel logs (dmesg), oom-kill events
- GPU-level: utilization, memory allocs/frees, kernel durations, memcpy times, PCIe saturation
- Traces: end-to-end request traces, per-component spans (tokenization, model-inference, post-process)
- Flamegraphs/pprof: top functions consuming CPU time; compare before/after
- Syscalls or context-switch spikes (perf top, eBPF traces)

Common root causes and quick signals:
- Kernel/driver update: simultaneous regressions across many services; check recent node pool upgrades and driver versions.
- Memory pressure / GC: rising RSS and GC pause times preceding latency spikes.
- Model changes / compilation differences: regression present only for specific models or after model rollout.
- Batching / scheduling changes: sudden queueing or higher per-request latency with same qps indicates scheduling regression.
- Network/NFS: I/O spikes or metadata server latencies often show up as tail latency spikes for checkpoints or model loads.

Escalation and communication:
- If triage can't find cause in 30–60 mins, escalate to on-call senior perf engineer and SRE lead.
- Create post-incident doc in Confluence: include timeline, graphs, root cause, mitigation, and follow-ups (actions). Use template: CONFLUENCE-RT/Perf-Postmortem-Template.

Runbook quick commands (examples):
- Compare p95 between clusters (Prometheus API): curl -g 'https://prom.redwood/api/v1/query?query=histogram_quantile(0.95,sum(rate(http_request_duration_seconds_bucket{route="/generate"}[5m])) by (le,cluster))'
- Collect pprof from a host: curl http://HOST:6060/debug/pprof/profile?seconds=30 > host.prof; go tool pprof -http=:8081 host.prof
- Warm-up workload (python): python infra/bench/run_load.py --concurrency 8 --requests 2000 --route /generate --model=gptx-v1 --target=http://HOST:8080

Post-triage RCA template (fill in):
- Incident id:
- Start / end times:
- Symptoms observed:
- Blast radius / affected customers:
- Root cause hypothesis and evidence:
- Mitigation applied:
- Long-term fix / action items:
- Owners and ETA:

Open TODOs / notes:
- Add automated bisect integration with CI to trigger PR bisect when canary deviates by >20% p95. (Marta to prototype)
- Improve canary labeling in Grafana to make comparisons one-click.
- Add more stable perf harness configs for low-variance runs (Samir).

References / related docs:
- perf-regression-triage-guide (short checklist) - see google_drive/shared_drives/engineering/serving-runtime/perf-regression-triage-guide.json
- perf-regression-alert-triage-workflow - older workflow doc in same folder
- Grafana perf overview: https://grafana.redwood.internal/d/serving-runtime/perf-overview
- Bisect harness repo: github.com/redwood-inference/serving-runtime/tools/perf-bisect

Notes to self / shorthand (working):
- watch for "hyper-quant" changes in compile step (these have bitten us before)
- when GPU memcpy jumps, check nvlink/PCIe congestion; sometimes node placement changes cause bad topology
- if bisect is noisy: try single-threaded perf microbench with same model weights to reduce noise
